correctness.rationale: For fixed labelled terminals in K_{a,b}, all xy cross-terminal edges are mandatory. Each same-shore pair has a shortest path through every vertex of the other shore, so after deletion any opposite nonterminal may retain at most one edge to that terminal shore. These are all the original geodesics, and the A_0 by B_0 edges affect none. Thus the classes of selected edges are independent; their factors are z^{xy}, H_x per B_0 vertex, H_y per A_0 vertex and 1+z per nonterminal-nonterminal edge. With no terminal neighbors the factor is 1; otherwise a minimum leaves exactly one, and no free edge can be in an inclusion-minimal set. This gives the minimum, count and exchange connectivity by changing one survivor at a time. The factorization has only nonpositive real roots and contiguous positive coefficient support, so Newton's inequalities give log-concavity and unimodality. When both terminal shores are occupied, the excess over x+y-1 is (b-1)(x-1)+(a-x)(y-1), zero in a non-star precisely for x=y=1. With terminals all on one shore the minimum is the opposite shore size times |T|-1; a star gives equality in every eligible placement, including when its center is a terminal.
